addons.purpose: Compact Claude Code-style tool output in the terminal (renderers only; it registers no tools).
clashes: It ships a second extension (`chrome`) that you may filter out in the package entry of `settings.json`.

addons.purpose: Background shell tasks for long-running commands (`bg_run`).
clashes: PI_BG_FEATURES=process is read when Pi starts, not at install: setup writes it to your shell profile (POSIX) or user environment (Windows) unless you pass --no-env.
Without `process`, its attribution extension takes over the global anthropic provider slot.
2.6.10 declares a Pi peer range of 0.81 to 0.84 while pi-foreman pins Pi 1.5.x; `/foreman doctor` reports the mismatch.

addons.purpose: Web fetch (`fetch`) and document conversion (`doc_to_md`) tools, plus opt-in session naming, header, fast mode and a provider stall watchdog.
clashes: It registers `fetch` and `doc_to_md` (always on). pi-foreman registers no tool of those names; its web-read rules gate `fetch`, and its role allowlists do not name either tool.

Session naming, the custom header (`/builtin-header`), fast mode (`/fast`) and the provider stall watchdog are opt-in in its own settings and stay off by default; pi-foreman has no equivalent of them.
Slack tools are opt-in too and need their own credentials.
It injects MEMORY.md, SCRATCHPAD.md and the daily logs into every turn and, unless PI_MEMORY_EXIT_SUMMARY=0 is set, makes one extra model call at session shutdown to write a summary.
`memory_search` needs the optional `qmd` command (npm i -g @tobilu/qmd); without it only that tool is unavailable and `/foreman doctor` says so (INFO). Installing works either way, on Windows too.
pi-foreman has no memory tools, so there is no name clash.
